statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-14677 (PostgreSQL 32-bit pltcl and plperl undersize allocations, via integer wraparound) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 16.15: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14677/ lists 16.15 as the fixed release for major version 16, and the 16.15 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.15/, include it. Alpine's postgresql16 16.15-r0 is the upgrade to upstream 16.15 and lists CVE-2026-14677 under its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from that APKBUILD and the upstream source release of the same version, and the postgres server binary in every published build (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports the matching PostgreSQL 16 release. PostgreSQL describes this flaw as affecting 32-bit builds of PL/Tcl and PL/Perl. This owner is published for Alpine 3.23 only on x86_64 and aarch64, which are 64-bit, and its PL/Perl and PL/Tcl modules (plperl.so in postgresql16-plperl, pltcl.so in postgresql16-pltcl) are built for those architectures. FIXED is recorded at the first build carrying the upstream fix, rather than NOT_AFFECTED, because the patched code ships in this owner and Alpine and PostgreSQL both list 16.15 as the fixed release. The earlier published builds for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0 and 16.14-r0) are built from earlier upstream releases, their server binaries report those older versions, and Alpine's secfixes do not list this CVE for them, so they are recorded as affected; 16.15-r0 and later carry the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14677 (PostgreSQL 32-bit pltcl and plperl undersize allocations, via integer wraparound) in 17.11 on the PostgreSQL 17 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14677/ lists 17.11 as the fixed release for major version 17, and the 17.11 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/b56cc7deb9af972226f7d6259248e00eb124069f on the REL_17_STABLE branch, which changes src/pl/plperl/SPI.xs, src/pl/plperl/plperl.c and src/pl/tcl/pltcl.c so that allocations sized by a multiplication use palloc_array(), which checks for overflow; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-14677, and it is in the REL_17_11 release tag and not in REL_17_10. PostgreSQL describes this flaw as affecting 32-bit builds of PL/Tcl and PL/Perl. This owner is published for Alpine 3.23 only on x86_64 and aarch64, which are 64-bit, and its PL/Perl and PL/Tcl modules, /usr/lib/postgresql17/plperl.so in postgresql17-plperl and /usr/lib/postgresql17/pltcl.so in postgresql17-pltcl, ship in every published build for those architectures. FIXED is recorded at the first build carrying the upstream fix, rather than NOT_AFFECTED, because the patched code ships in this owner and PostgreSQL and Alpine both list 17.11 as the fixed release. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD, currently https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the source files this fix changes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql17/postgres, in every published postgresql17 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 report PostgreSQL 17.11 and 17.12 and carry the fix, while the earlier builds 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0 and 17.10-r0 report 17.7, 17.8, 17.9 and 17.10 and are affected. This fix adds no distinctive message string, so the per-build evidence is the version each server binary reports. 17.11-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix. Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-14677 under its 17.11-r0 secfixes.

CVE-2026-14677 (PostgreSQL 32-bit pltcl and plperl undersize allocations, via integer wraparound): https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14677/ lists 18.6 as the fixed release for major version 18, and the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, list this CVE. The fix on the REL_18_STABLE branch is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/028ee716a7902bd2a68843a5d317a6821a0500e2 (Security: CVE-2026-14677, in tag REL_18_6 and not in REL_18_4), which changes src/pl/plperl/SPI.xs, src/pl/plperl/plperl.c and src/pl/tcl/pltcl.c so that allocations sized by a multiplication use palloc_array(), which in PostgreSQL 18 expands to the overflow-checking palloc_mul(). PostgreSQL describes the flaw as affecting 32-bit builds. This owner is published for Alpine 3.23 only on x86_64 and aarch64, which are 64-bit, but its PL/Perl and PL/Tcl modules, /usr/lib/postgresql18/plperl.so in postgresql18-plperl and /usr/lib/postgresql18/pltcl.so in postgresql18-pltcl, ship in every published build, so FIXED is recorded at the first build carrying the upstream fix rather than NOT_AFFECTED: the patched code ships in this owner and PostgreSQL lists 18.6 as the fixed release. PostgreSQL 18.5 was never released (the 18.6 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/, say so), so although Alpine's security database lists this CVE for postgresql18 under 18.5-r0, this owner has no 18.5-r0 build and its first build that carries the fix is 18.6-r0. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD from the 3.23-stable branch of aports (current revision https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD) and the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version; none of the patches that APKBUILD applies, at any revision used for these builds, changes the files this fix changes. As of 2026-11-28 the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes builds of source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64. We read every one of them on both architectures, with package checksums verified against the repository index, and in each the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres, reports the PostgreSQL release matching its package version. Other PL/Perl and PL/Tcl changes in the same release also touch these files, so no symbol marks this fix on its own, and the per-build evidence is the release each server binary reports. 18.6-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 that carries the fix, and 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 carry it. The earlier published builds (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0 and 18.4-r0) are built from PostgreSQL releases before the fix and are affected.

The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.24 are built with Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD from the 3.24-stable branch of aports (current revision https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/33a57d3919ee0227231f5a3e599540514584e309/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD) and the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version; none of the patches that APKBUILD applies, at any revision used for these builds, changes the files this fix changes. As of 2026-11-28 the DHI Alpine 3.24 package repository publishes builds of source postgresql18 at 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64. We read every one of them on both architectures, with package checksums verified against the repository index, and in each the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres, reports the PostgreSQL release matching its package version. Other PL/Perl and PL/Tcl changes in the same release also touch these files, so no symbol marks this fix on its own, and the per-build evidence is the release each server binary reports. 18.6-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.24 that carries the fix, and 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 carry it. The earlier published build (18.4-r0) is built from PostgreSQL releases before the fix and is affected.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14677, integer wraparound in 32-bit builds of PL/Tcl and PL/Perl that undersizes an allocation and writes out of bounds, in 17.11. Within major version 17, releases before 17.11 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14677/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.11/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.11-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6438-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-14677. The fixed version is this owner's first rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1, which packages PostgreSQL 17.11 and is no longer in the repository. Every build published now carries the fix: the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.11 in the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 and in the 17.11-1 build, and PostgreSQL 17.12 in the 17.12-0 build and in the rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1, on amd64 and arm64. The earlier rebuild of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, packages PostgreSQL 17.10; it is affected and sorts below the fixed version.
